papers.title: Attention-Guided Transformer Network for Polyp Segmentation in Colonoscopy Images
papers.problem: Polyp segmentation is challenged by varying polyp shapes, sizes, and unclear boundaries in colonoscopy images.
papers.methodology: Transformer encoder with multi-scale attention decoder for local and global context fusion.
contributions: Novel multi-scale attention decoder that captures boundary details
State-of-the-art performance on Kvasir-SEG and CVC-ClinicDB
Open-source code and pretrained models released
limitations: High computational cost compared to lightweight CNNs
Only evaluated on public datasets, not clinical data
papers.summary: This paper proposes a transformer-based architecture with a multi-scale attention decoder for polyp segmentation. The model achieves 0.923 Dice on Kvasir-SEG, outperforming prior methods, especially on polyps with unclear boundaries. However, the approach has high computational requirements and has not been validated for real-time clinical deployment.

papers.title: Efficient U-Net with Depthwise Separable Convolutions for Real-Time Polyp Segmentation
papers.problem: Existing polyp segmentation models are too heavy for real-time clinical deployment on edge devices.
papers.methodology: Lightweight U-Net using depthwise separable convolutions to reduce parameters while maintaining accuracy.
contributions: Ultra-lightweight architecture (2.1M parameters) suitable for edge deployment
Real-time performance at 120 FPS on standard GPU
Competitive accuracy with 93% fewer parameters than standard U-Net
limitations: Lower accuracy compared to transformer-based methods (0.891 vs 0.923)
No clinical validation or deployment on actual hardware
papers.summary: This paper presents EfficientU-Net, a lightweight CNN using depthwise separable convolutions that achieves 0.891 Dice on Kvasir-SEG while running at 120 FPS with only 2.1M parameters. It is designed for real-time clinical deployment but has lower accuracy than transformer-based approaches and lacks clinical validation.

papers.title: Cross-Domain Polyp Segmentation via Style Transfer and Domain Adaptation
papers.problem: Polyp segmentation models fail to generalize across datasets from different medical centers due to domain shift.
papers.methodology: Domain adaptation framework combining style transfer, domain discriminator, and style-matching loss.
contributions: Style transfer approach reduces domain gap between colonoscopy datasets
12% Dice improvement on cross-domain evaluation without target labels
limitations: Style transfer may alter clinically relevant features
Evaluated only on polyp datasets, not other modalities
papers.summary: This paper addresses domain shift in polyp segmentation by proposing a style transfer and domain adaptation framework. It achieves 12% Dice improvement when transferring from Kvasir-SEG to ETIS-Larib without target domain labels. The approach reduces annotation burden but may alter clinically relevant features through style transfer.
